title: False presupposition: what many deny is not thereby uncertain for the sound
source_text: XX. Sed ut istius sophismatis vanitas clarius appareat, notandum in eo multa praesupponi quae omnino falsa sunt. Et primo quidem supponit illud omne nobis esse dubium & incertum quod a multis negatur, & de quo sunt multi qui dubitant. At si hoc admittatur nihil prorsus certum remanebit. Vix enim quicquam est tam certum & evidens, de quo non fuerit a multis dubitatum; imo quod a multis negatum non fuerit. Ita nobis certum non erit ex caeli & terrae aspectu Deum esse, quoniam Epicurei & Athei hoc negant. Neque prima principia scientiarum nobis certa erunt, & indubitata, quoniam Pyrrhonii, qui assensum omnem tollebant, de istis quoque dubitarunt. Neque Pontificiis, ut diximus, certa erit Ecclesiae suae authoritas, quoniam a reliquis Christianis negatur. Itaque dicendum id de quo immerito dubitatur, & quod sine ratione negatur, non desinere certum esse recte sentientibus. Nec enim hominum male feriatorum, perversorum atque stultorum error & dubitatio circa res in se certas, quicquam obest certitudini hominum sani judicii, & quorum mens recte affecta est.
pass_a_gloss: But so that the vanity of this sophism may appear more clearly, it is to be noted that in it many things are presupposed that are altogether false. And first indeed it supposes that everything is doubtful and uncertain for us which is denied by many, and about which there are many who doubt. But if this is admitted, nothing at all certain will remain. For scarcely anything is so certain and evident about which there has not been doubt by many; indeed which has not been denied by many. Thus it will not be certain for us from the sight of heaven and earth that God is, because Epicureans and Atheists deny this. Nor will the first principles of the sciences be certain and undoubted for us, because the Pyrrhonians, who took away all assent, doubted about those also. Nor, as we have said, will the authority of their Church be certain for the Pontificians, because it is denied by the rest of Christians. Therefore it must be said that that about which there is undeserved doubt, and which is denied without reason, does not cease to be certain for those who judge rightly. For the error and doubt of ill-employed, perverse, and foolish men about things certain in themselves does not at all hinder the certainty of men of sound judgment whose mind is rightly affected.
pass_b_english: To see the sophism's emptiness more clearly, note how many false things it assumes.

First it assumes that whatever many deny, or many doubt, is doubtful and uncertain for us. Admit that, and nothing certain remains. Almost nothing so certain and evident has escaped doubt — or flat denial — from many.

Then it would not be certain from the sight of heaven and earth that God is, because Epicureans and atheists deny it. First principles of the sciences would not be certain, because Pyrrhonians who suspended all assent doubted them too. And Rome's own church authority would not be certain for Romanists, because the rest of Christians deny it.

What is doubted without desert, and denied without reason, does not cease to be certain for those who judge rightly. The error and doubt of idle, perverse, foolish people about things certain in themselves do not touch the certainty of sound minds rightly disposed.

lemmas.gloss: Pyrrhonians who took away all assent
